title: Latent-prefix cache scratchpad
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick lab notes after reading a few papers and talking with Omar at the NeurIPS local meetup. Trying to distill practical ideas we can prototype in the serving runtime.
- Goal: find low-compute, low-latency cache/prefix mechanisms that (a) reduce token cost on long-tail sessions, (b) don't bloat memory for Dedicated pools, and (c) gracefully degrade with quantized models.

High-level observation (working hypothesis):
- A small, learnable "latent prefix" (dense vector per conversation or per user segment) combined with a compact micro-KV (hashed or compressed) can capture repeated local context without storing full token histories.
- For many product flows (support chat, code edit sessions), the effective context that matters for generation is low-rank or compressible. So we can store compressed summaries and apply as prefix at generation time.

Papers / threads skimmed (short notes):
- "Latent Cache for Transformers" (arXiv:2808.04567) - proposes a learned projection from past hidden states -> small set of prefix vectors, applied at inference as an extra set of cached attention keys/values. Claims similar perplexity to 1k token KV cache using only 8 prefix vectors.
  - key idea: train projection with distillation from full-context model.
  - tradeoffs: extra matmul at decode time to expand latent->key/val; cheap if projection dims small.
- "Prefix-Tuning++: Sparse and Adaptive Prefixes" (paper notes in author slides)
  - variable-length prefix selection using a lightweight selector network per request. Useful for per-route adaptation.
- KV compression by product quantization / chunked Huffman on top of keys (2027 workshop notes)
  - good for storage but slows random access; best when access pattern is locality-heavy (recent keys reused).

Ideas to try (ranked):
1) Micro-latent prefix + tiny hashed KV: prototype in serving runtime branch (opt-kv).
   - For each session keep: up to 32 latent vectors (d=512) + small hashed KV for raw tokens (for exact repeats).
   - On request: expand latent vectors -> keys/vals (single matmul) and append to attention cache before decoding.
   - Fall back: if CPU budget low, skip latent expansion and use only hashed KV.
2) Learn selector that picks 0..N latent vectors per request based on first 2 tokens and metadata (route, user-tier).
3) Offline distillation pass: distill full 4096-token context into variable-size latent prefix using teacher-student. Store per-conversation latent in user store (encrypted).
4) KV compression layer: implement simple 8-bit PQ + bloom filter for membership test. Evaluate speed/memory tradeoffs.

Experiment plan (first pass):
- Baseline: current per-token KV cache (no compression) + window = 2048. Measure (p50 latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory).
- Proto A: latents only (no raw KV), 8 latents, distillation trained on 1000 chats. Measure quality (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and human eval on 100 prompts).
- Proto B: latents + hashed KV (LRU up to 256 entries). Compare to baseline on cost and latency.
- Proto C: latents + PQ compress keys (4 bits) + bloom filter. Measure decode throughput when many cache hits and when cold.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Latent-only: <2% relative quality drop on our eval set vs baseline while reducing GPU memory use for cache by >= 4x.
- Latent+hashed: <5% latency overhead at p95 and token cost reduced by >= 20% on long sessions (>2k tokens).
- Compression: decoding throughput drop <= 10% vs uncompressed when hit rate > 70%. If slower, rethink on-device decompression cost.

Open questions / risks:
- Security/privacy: storing compressed latent summaries could still leak private info. Need alignment with privacy team. (Loop in security early).
- Determinism and debugging: latent vectors are not human interpretable; harder to debug hallucinations / failure modes. Need deterministic seeds + audit pipeline.
- Quantized model compatibility: will 8-bit PQ keys degrade attention matching? test on quantized weights first.
- Metric sensitivity: our eval sets might underweight long-term conversational coherence. Add human A/B tests.

Engineering notes (runtime impact):
- Implementation knobs: per-session store, TTL, eviction policy, sync frequency between VMs. Prefer local ephemeral store for Dedicated nodes; sync to central blobstore only at session end or checkpoint.
- Memory accounting: 32 latents * 512 dims * 4 bytes = 64KB per session (fp32). With 10k concurrent sessions -> 640MB. If we store fp16 or int8, cost drops.
- CPU work at decode: latent->kv expansion = matmul of (num_latents x latent_dim) x (latent_dim x kv_dim) -> small but must be in hot path. Consider caching expanded KV pre-token to avoid repeated matmuls for multi-token decode.

Short to-dos (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Sync with Omar for a small distillation dataset (he has 3k anonymized customer sessions).
- [ ] Prototype decoder-side latent expansion in local runtime branch (PR scaffolded: opt-kv/latent-expand).
- [ ] Quick eval harness: 200 synthetic long sessions (inference only) to measure p95 latency.
- [ ] File a security note and schedule 30-min call with security/compliance.

Notes-to-self / heuristics:
- When hit rate low (<30%), latent-only will likely hurt quality; fallback to short rolling window.
- For high-reuse routes (support macros, code completions), hashed exact-match KV is cheap and effective.
- Keep number of latents small (<=32) and vector dim <= 1024 to avoid matmul scaling. Prefer fp16 storage for Dedicated.

Reference snippets to copy into PR description later:
- "We implement a compact latent prefix mechanism that converts per-session history into 8-32 learned vectors. At decode time these vectors are expanded into attention keys/values and appended to the runtime cache. This reduces memory footprint and amortizes long-term context into a small, composable prefix. Fallback heuristics enable graceful degradation on low CPU budgets."

Random brain dump (short):
- Could combine with Optimize's prompt-slicer to only expand latents for routes where evaluation shows benefit.
- Potential synergy with rollout policies: roll out latent-prefix per-route A/B to measure quality and cost.
- Consider privacy preserving distillation: train distiller on hashed token ngrams to remove PII.

End notes: this is messy — intentionally. Save as scratchpad. Will turn into a short RFC if early results look promising.
